flavor_text: Two wins on Tour and a high ranking in the key putting stats made him a near-lock pick. Ryder Cup debut.

name: Daniel Berger
flavor_text: Clinched a win at Pebble Beach with an eagle on the 18th. Ryder Cup debut, went 2-1-0.

name: Paul Casey
flavor_text: Cooled badly after a hot March; an automatic World Points qualifier who went 0-4 in the blowout.

name: Lee Westwood
flavor_text: The "last man in," sweating the final qualifying spot 24 years after his Cup debut. Got married to his caddie days before flying to Wisconsin.

name: Sergio Garcia
flavor_text: Harrington called him a no-brainer pick months in advance. Paired with Rahm to post Europe's only bright spot of the week.

name: Scottie Scheffler
flavor_text: Still without a Tour win, but top-19-or-better in six straight majors made him the surprise final automatic-feeling pick. Beat Jon Rahm in Sunday singles. Ryder Cup debut.

name: Patrick Reed
flavor_text: "Captain America," in every US team since 2014, left out after bilateral pneumonia and an ankle injury wiped out his playoff run. Stricker said he "lost sleep" over the call.

name: Webb Simpson
flavor_text: 13th in the standings; six top-10s and a reputation as a steady team-room presence weren't enough in a year USA leaned young.

name: Kevin Na
flavor_text: Hot down the stretch with a T1 at the Tour Championship, but his lack of length was viewed as a poor fit for Whistling Straits.

name: Will Zalatoris
flavor_text: Masters runner-up in his rookie year and a ball-striking machine, but ranked 122nd in Tour putting; that flaw kept him off a young, deep team.

name: Sam Burns
flavor_text: First Tour win and a breakout season, but his case never built the buzz of the other contenders this cycle.

name: Jason Kokrak
flavor_text: Took 233 starts to win his first Tour event, then won again 17 starts later. A great course fit, but no team-golf history to lean on.

name: Kevin Kisner
flavor_text: A social-media cause celebre for a pick that never had real traction. Excels on poa annua greens but lacked the season to back it up.

name: Justin Rose
flavor_text: The "13th man." A closing 65 at Wentworth wasn't enough; Harrington called it "incredibly difficult" to leave him out for Lowry and Poulter's pedigree.

name: Victor Perez
flavor_text: Sat 6th on the European points list deep into the qualifying window, part of the genuine bubble conversation.

name: Robert MacIntyre
flavor_text: 7th on the European points list as a 25-year-old; two years away from his actual Cup debut.

name: Guido Migliozzi
flavor_text: An Italian rookie deep in the European bubble conversation, two years ahead of his country hosting the Cup.

name: Bryson DeChambeau
flavor_text: Two wins and a scientific approach to the game. Ryder Cup debut went winless across three matches.

name: Phil Mickelson
flavor_text: First time failing to qualify on points since 1995, picked anyway on reputation alone. Set the Ryder Cup record for career losses going 0-2.

name: Webb Simpson
flavor_text: Quiet, efficient green play paired with Bubba Watson produced one of Team USA's few highlights of the week.

name: Bubba Watson
flavor_text: Among the longest hitters in the game; paired well with Simpson but the team around him struggled all week.

name: Sergio Garcia
flavor_text: One of his worst seasons ever, missed cuts in over half his 2018 starts, but Bjorn called him "the heartbeat of the team" and picked him regardless. Became the all-time Ryder Cup points leader.

name: Alex Noren
flavor_text: Ryder Cup debut; clinched the winning point with a long birdie putt on the 18th green.

name: Henrik Stenson
flavor_text: Elbow issues clouded his selection, but Bjorn said Rose "would find it difficult" without him. Went perfect 3-0-0 in his fourth Cup.

name: Matt Kuchar
flavor_text: Furyk "would have loved" to have him for his experience and team-room humor, but a final-round 74 in Boston dropped him out of contention entirely.

name: Xander Schauffele
flavor_text: Rookie of the Year in 2017 with two wins; in the conversation for a pick but a missed cut at the Northern Trust hurt his case.

name: Kevin Kisner
flavor_text: A strong fit for Le Golf National's tight fairways on paper, but cold putting down the stretch cost him the final spot.

name: Brian Harman
flavor_text: Quietly inside the top 20 in points for most of the season; never built the late-season case to force the pick.

name: Brandt Snedeker
flavor_text: Shot a 59 to win the Wyndham Championship, then withdrew from the next event with back spasms at the worst possible time.

name: Zach Johnson
flavor_text: Veteran of five prior Cups, in the late mix on experience alone before ultimately joining the team room as a vice-captain instead.

name: Matt Wallace
flavor_text: Won three times on the European Tour, including the week before selection, but Bjorn passed on a sixth rookie in favor of experience.

name: Matt Fitzpatrick
flavor_text: A strong contender on paper, but his actual Cup debut wouldn't arrive until 2021.

name: Rafa Cabrera-Bello
flavor_text: A 2016 Cup rookie whose case for a repeat pick faded as the rookies already on the team piled up.

name: Russell Knox
flavor_text: Had a chance to impress Bjorn in the final qualifying weeks and didn't take it.

name: Jimmy Walker
flavor_text: Won the PGA Championship in 2016. Ryder Cup debut as an automatic qualifier.

name: Brooks Koepka
flavor_text: Ryder Cup debut, paired well with Brandt Snedeker to post a 3-1-0 week and announce himself as a future fixture on the team.

name: Brandt Snedeker
flavor_text: Perfect 3-0-0 week alongside Koepka, the only American to go through Hazeltine unbeaten.

name: Zach Johnson
flavor_text: Veteran presence on a young team; went 2-1-0 in his fifth Cup appearance.

name: Matt Kuchar
flavor_text: Trusted captain's pick on experience; went 2-2-0 in his fourth appearance.

name: Rafa Cabrera Bello
flavor_text: Ryder Cup debut alongside Garcia; went undefeated in team play before falling in singles.

name: Andy Sullivan
flavor_text: Ryder Cup debut as an automatic qualifier; a tough week against a rampant US side.

name: Matt Fitzpatrick
flavor_text: At 22, the youngest player at Hazeltine. Ryder Cup debut went winless across two matches.

name: Martin Kaymer
flavor_text: The man who clinched the Miracle at Medinah four years earlier; a rough week at Hazeltine in his fourth Cup.

name: J.B. Holmes
flavor_text: Power player returning to the team eight years after his 2008 debut; paired with Ryan Moore in the fourball sessions.

name: Justin Thomas
flavor_text: In the Tour Championship "tryout" conversation alongside Daniel Berger for a young pick; his Cup debut would have to wait two more years.

name: Daniel Berger
flavor_text: Said making the Ryder Cup, like his father's Davis Cup tennis career, was a personal goal; close but not quite there as a 23-year-old.

name: Kevin Chappell
flavor_text: Playing well in the run-up to selection, part of the genuine late-season conversation for the final pick.

name: Jason Dufner
flavor_text: A major champion with the steady, efficient game that fits team golf, but not enough season to force the pick.

name: Gary Woodland
flavor_text: Long off the tee and in the late-season conversation, but the season-long résumé wasn't quite enough.

name: Kevin Kisner
flavor_text: A name that comes up nearly every cycle for his match-play toughness; another near-miss in 2016.

name: Kevin Na
flavor_text: A perennial bubble name; his short game keeps him in the conversation every cycle without quite breaking through.

name: Jim Furyk
flavor_text: Doubled as a vice-captain while nursing a wrist injury; Love seriously weighed the old-veteran card before going younger.

name: Russell Knox
flavor_text: Genuinely unlucky: his 2015 WGC win came before his European Tour membership counted points, costing him the automatic spot he'd otherwise have claimed. Won the Travelers in 2016 anyway and still didn't get a pick.

name: Soren Kjeldsen
flavor_text: Consistent veteran in the European mix, edged out by Clarke's preference for proven Cup pedigree.

name: Jimmy Walker
flavor_text: Ryder Cup debut; one of two American rookies who held their own at Gleneagles, going 1-1-3.

name: Zach Johnson
flavor_text: Got the last automatic spot by making the cut at the PGA Championship despite a closing 77.

name: Keegan Bradley
flavor_text: Half of the "Redeem Team" trio after 2012 Medinah heartbreak; the redemption never quite arrived.

name: Webb Simpson
flavor_text: Lobbied his way onto the team with a 4 a.m. text to Watson; the gamble produced little, just a half point.

name: Hunter Mahan
flavor_text: A win at The Barclays fueled his case; part of the "Redeem Team" group that fell short again.

name: Martin Kaymer
flavor_text: Chipped in for the win over Bubba Watson that put Europe on the brink of clinching at home.

name: Thomas Bjorn
flavor_text: Automatic qualifier in his first Cup appearance since 2002, a 12-year wait finally rewarded.

name: Lee Westwood
flavor_text: Edged out Tyrrell Hatton and Soren Kjeldsen for McGinley's third pick on reputation and pedigree.

name: Billy Horschel
flavor_text: Watson passed on him for the final pick; Horschel then won the BMW Championship and the Tour Championship to claim the FedEx Cup the same month, prompting the PGA to push back future pick deadlines.

name: Steve Stricker
flavor_text: Served as a vice-captain instead; a limited 2014 schedule kept him out of pick contention.

name: Chris Kirk
flavor_text: Briefly atop the FedEx Cup standings alongside Horschel before cooling off at the wrong time.

name: Jason Dufner
flavor_text: Climbed to the last automatic spot before a neck injury forced him to withdraw, opening the door for Zach Johnson.

name: Brendon Todd
flavor_text: Outranked several captain's pick candidates in points but never entered the real selection conversation.

name: Joost Luiten
flavor_text: Highest-ranked Dutch player in the conversation, but a long way from a genuine pick.

name: Miguel Angel Jimenez
flavor_text: At 50, still ranked inside the world's top 40; ultimately joined McGinley's five-strong vice-captain team instead of playing.

name: Zach Johnson
flavor_text: Won the Match Play small-ball event again on form; one of the better American performers in a losing effort.

name: Matt Kuchar
flavor_text: Among the most consistent Americans across the first two days before the Sunday collapse.

name: Steve Stricker
flavor_text: Paired with a struggling Tiger Woods; a rare winless week capped by a three-putt that opened the door for Kaymer's clincher.

name: Paul Lawrie
flavor_text: First Cup appearance in 13 years; part of the historic five-straight-wins start to Europe's Sunday comeback.

name: Francesco Molinari
flavor_text: Faced Tiger Woods in the final match; Woods conceded the closing putt after Europe had already retained the Cup, sealing the half point and the outright win.

name: Martin Kaymer
flavor_text: Nearly fell out of the team during the last week of qualifying; hit the six-foot putt on the 18th that retained the Cup, the defining moment of the Miracle at Medinah.

name: Hunter Mahan
flavor_text: Won the Match Play Championship with a dominant final win over Rory McIlroy; the toughest call Love had to make, but a cold five months sealed his exclusion.

name: Rickie Fowler
flavor_text: Won at Quail Hollow but struggled in the majors down the stretch; close friends with Webb Simpson but it was not enough to get the pick.

name: Bo Van Pelt
flavor_text: An experience case missed his only real shot by not playing quite well enough down the stretch.

name: Robert Garrigus
flavor_text: Long off the tee, but a recent history of late-round collapses worked against him.

name: Nick Watney
flavor_text: Won The Barclays against one of the strongest fields of the year, but faded immediately after and lost momentum at the worst time.

name: Bill Haas
flavor_text: Among the players under serious consideration deep into the FedEx Cup playoffs, but the picks went elsewhere.

name: Steve Stricker
flavor_text: Paired with Tiger Woods for a dominant 3-1-0 week, the strongest American pairing of the Cup.

name: Zach Johnson
flavor_text: Quietly efficient across the week, one of the better American performers in a narrow loss.

name: Tiger Woods
flavor_text: Returned from personal turmoil to anchor the team alongside Stricker; one of his strongest Cup performances by record.

name: Stewart Cink
flavor_text: Famously the captain's pick Pavin forgot to name at the opening ceremony; went unbeaten across four matches anyway.

name: Francesco Molinari
flavor_text: Cup debut alongside brother Edoardo, becoming the second pair of brothers to play on the same Ryder Cup team.

name: Miguel Angel Jimenez
flavor_text: His win over Bubba Watson pushed Europe to a 13-9 lead and the brink of regaining the Cup outright.

name: Peter Hanson
flavor_text: Cup debut paired with Jimenez; contributed one point as a rookie in a tight contest.

name: Padraig Harrington
flavor_text: Got the pick over a heartbroken Paul Casey, a moment that became one of the most talked-about selections of the era.

name: Paul Casey
flavor_text: World No. 7 heading into selection, in tears after being passed over. Found out he'd been left off while playing alongside the man who got the pick instead, noticing the celebration mid-round. Called it a scar that lingered for years.

name: Anthony Kim
flavor_text: Ryder Cup debut; opened Sunday singles by routing Sergio Garcia 5&4 to set the tone for the entire session.

name: Justin Leonard
flavor_text: The man who clinched Brookline 1999 with the putt that triggered the green invasion. Returned to the team nearly a decade later and went 2-1-1.

name: Ben Curtis
flavor_text: Azinger picked him on heart as much as resume, citing the way Curtis had fought back from a down spell to win twice that year.

name: J.B. Holmes
flavor_text: Grew up nearby and knew Valhalla better than anyone in the field; beat Phil Mickelson in a playoff earlier that year on his way to the pick.

name: Chad Campbell
flavor_text: Third straight Cup, first as a captain's pick; closed out the clinching point with a win over Padraig Harrington.

name: Miguel Angel Jimenez
flavor_text: Lost the deciding singles point to Jim Furyk on the 17th hole, sealing the American victory.

name: Justin Rose
flavor_text: Ryder Cup debut as one of the last three European automatic qualifiers; went 3-1-0, the best record on a losing side.

name: Paul Casey
flavor_text: Captain's pick alongside Poulter; would not play another Cup until a decade later, in 2018.

name: Tiger Woods
flavor_text: Led the points list outright but was recovering from reconstructive knee surgery after winning the U.S. Open. Azinger said he saw no positive way to spin not having him on the team.

name: Scott Verplank
flavor_text: 33rd in the final standings but a 4-1-0 record in his two prior Cups made him a favorite of teammates who did make the team.

name: Woody Austin
flavor_text: Finished 10th in the points standings and would have qualified automatically under the old system before Azinger added extra picks.

name: Rocco Mediate
flavor_text: Became an overnight sensation after a 19-hole U.S. Open playoff loss to Tiger Woods, but it came too late to change the picks.

name: Brandt Snedeker
flavor_text: In the outer conversation as a rookie name, but the picks went to more proven veterans.

name: Darren Clarke
flavor_text: Won twice in the four months before selection and had played five straight Cups, but Faldo overlooked him for Poulter and Casey.

name: Chris DiMarco
flavor_text: Fourth straight Cup appearance; part of a USA team that managed only six wins across all 28 matches.

name: J.J. Henry
flavor_text: Ryder Cup debut; lined up a 25-foot putt to halve his singles match when a streaker ran across the green, and Paul McGinley conceded the putt out of sportsmanship rather than let the moment decide it.

name: David Toms
flavor_text: Third straight Cup appearance on a US team that managed only one winning record outside Tiger Woods and Scott Verplank.

name: Robert Karlsson
flavor_text: Ryder Cup debut on a dominant European side that won every session of the week.

name: Paul McGinley
flavor_text: Conceded a halving putt to J.J. Henry after a streaker disrupted the moment, costing Europe what could have been the largest margin in Ryder Cup history.

name: Colin Montgomerie
flavor_text: Veteran leader in his eighth Cup, drawing on 37 European Tour wins to anchor the team room.

name: Jose Maria Olazabal
flavor_text: The last of eight Cup selections; closed out his playing career with a perfect 3-0-0 week, including the win that beat a struggling Phil Mickelson.

name: Lee Westwood
flavor_text: Hand-picked by Woosnam to partner the grieving Darren Clarke; the pairing went a combined 6-0-2, the best captain's-pick partnership in Cup history to that point.

name: Jay Haas
flavor_text: Ryder Cup debut at age 50, the oldest US rookie in modern history; paired with DiMarco for the team's lone Saturday foursomes win.

name: Fred Funk
flavor_text: Ryder Cup debut at age 48, the second-oldest US rookie in modern history; went winless across three matches.

name: Davis Love III
flavor_text: Ended his playing Ryder Cup career with a half against good friend Darren Clarke, the two sharing a hug and a cigar by the 18th green.

name: Kenny Perry
flavor_text: Two wins that season earned the call; closed his week losing to Westwood's clinching par putt.

name: Chris Riley
flavor_text: Ryder Cup debut; a clutch 7-foot par putt on the 18th kept the US from being shut out on the opening day.

name: David Toms
flavor_text: Second straight Cup; pushed Montgomerie to a tense singles finish that ultimately confirmed Europe's win.

name: Miguel Angel Jimenez
flavor_text: Lost his singles match to Chris DiMarco late, the only blemish in an otherwise dominant European week.

name: Thomas Levet
flavor_text: Ryder Cup debut paired primarily with Jimenez on a team stacked deep with rookies who barely needed to play.

name: Paul McGinley
flavor_text: Paired with countryman Padraig Harrington for a dominant all-Dublin foursomes win over Woods and Love that turned the tide of the week.

name: David Duval
flavor_text: Second Cup appearance on a US team that struggled to convert across the board.

name: Scott Hoch
flavor_text: Squared off with Montgomerie in the opening singles match and never got the lead.

name: Hal Sutton
flavor_text: Lost his singles match to Bernhard Langer, who later captained the Americans against him two cups on.

name: Thomas Bjorn
flavor_text: Won his singles match to help confirm Europe's win; first Cup appearance in five years.

name: Bernhard Langer
flavor_text: His tenth and final Cup as a player went out a winner, beating Hal Sutton in singles to cap a 3-0-1 week.

name: Pierre Fulke
flavor_text: Ryder Cup debut as a Swedish automatic qualifier in a team stacked with experience.

name: Niclas Fasth
flavor_text: Ryder Cup debut; his singles match against Paul Azinger went down to the wire as Europe's win became official elsewhere on the course.

name: Phillip Price
flavor_text: Ranked 119th in the world, the lowest-ranked player in the field, but produced one of the great Ryder Cup upsets by routing Phil Mickelson in singles.

name: Jesper Parnevik
flavor_text: His final Ryder Cup match ended in a half after Tiger Woods, already irrelevant to the result, conceded the closing putt as a gesture of sportsmanship.

name: Tiger Woods
flavor_text: Second Cup; closed out Andrew Coltart 3&2 in singles as the American comeback gathered steam, though a marshal-trodden ball cost his playing partner a hole along the way.

name: David Duval
flavor_text: Ryder Cup debut; argued publicly that players should be compensated for the event, fuel for the pre-match controversy that defined the week.

name: Payne Stewart
flavor_text: Said before the matches that Europe should be caddying for the Americans, then conceded his singles match to Montgomerie on the final hole as a gesture after the Scot endured relentless crowd abuse all week. Died in a plane crash weeks later.

name: Davis Love III
flavor_text: Routed Jean Van de Velde 6&5 in singles on the day of the great comeback, going unbeaten across his three matches.

name: Mark O'Meara
flavor_text: Lost a tense singles match to Padraig Harrington on the final day, one of the few American defeats during the historic comeback session.

name: Hal Sutton
flavor_text: Returned after a 12-year absence from the team and went 3-1-1, beating Darren Clarke in the Sunday singles charge.

name: Justin Leonard
flavor_text: Holed a 45-foot birdie putt on the 17th hole against Olazabal to seal the half point that won back the Cup, triggering a premature on-green celebration that became one of the sport's most debated moments of sportsmanship.

name: Jim Furyk
flavor_text: Chipped in from near a pond on Friday to square a match, then closed out Sergio Garcia 4&3 in singles to push the comeback within a half-point of completion.

name: Phil Mickelson
flavor_text: Beat Jarmo Sandelin in singles as part of the historic six-match opening sweep that launched the American comeback.

name: Jeff Maggert
flavor_text: Called the US team the 12 best players in the world before the matches began, then lost the week's final singles match to Paul Lawrie 4&3.

name: Tom Lehman
flavor_text: Chipped in at the very first hole of the week to give the Americans an early spark, then opened the Sunday comeback by beating Lee Westwood 3&2.

name: Steve Pate
flavor_text: Beat Miguel Angel Jimenez 2&1 in singles, pushing the Americans within a half-point of reclaiming the Cup.

name: Colin Montgomerie
flavor_text: Endured relentless abuse from the Brookline crowd, severe enough that his own father walked off the course rather than listen to it. Stewart conceded their singles match on the final hole afterward as a gesture of sportsmanship.

name: Lee Westwood
flavor_text: Partnered Darren Clarke to upset Tiger Woods and David Duval, the top two ranked players in the world, on the opening day.

name: Darren Clarke
flavor_text: Helped upset Woods and Duval alongside Westwood on day one, but lost his singles match to Hal Sutton during the Sunday collapse.

name: Paul Lawrie
flavor_text: Ryder Cup debut off the back of his Open Championship win; struck the opening tee shot of the entire week and closed it out by beating Jeff Maggert 4&3 in the final match on the course.

name: Miguel Angel Jimenez
flavor_text: Ryder Cup debut; lost his singles match to Steve Pate as the American comeback gathered pace.

name: Jose Maria Olazabal
flavor_text: Led Justin Leonard 4-up through 11 holes in their singles match before Leonard's comeback produced the famous 17th-hole putt and the green invasion that followed; Olazabal then missed his own putt to confirm the American win.

name: Sergio Garcia
flavor_text: Ryder Cup debut at 19, the youngest player at Brookline; eagled the 14th hole alongside Parnevik in one of the week's best team matches before losing the deciding singles point to Jim Furyk.

name: Jarmo Sandelin
flavor_text: Ryder Cup debut; held in reserve by captain Mark James for the first two days before losing his singles match to Phil Mickelson.

name: Jean Van de Velde
flavor_text: Selected off the back of his infamous Open Championship collapse earlier that year; held in reserve like fellow rookies Sandelin and Coltart before a 6&5 singles loss to Davis Love III.

name: Padraig Harrington
flavor_text: Beat Mark O'Meara in the second-to-last singles match, but it arrived too late to halt the American comeback.

name: Andrew Coltart
flavor_text: Ryder Cup debut as a captain's pick over Bernhard Langer and Robert Karlsson; lost his lone match to Tiger Woods 3&2 after a controversial lost ball along the way.

name: Jesper Parnevik
flavor_text: Holed out for eagle with a 9-iron from 135 yards alongside Garcia in one of the week's best team matches, then beat David Duval in singles before the Americans' run took hold.

name: Bryson DeChambeau
flavor_text: 54th on the points list after his move to LIV cut off access to PGA Tour points, but riding a hot streak into selection week. Zach Johnson didn't even call to say he'd been left off, a slight that stung more than the snub itself.

name: Sergio Garcia
flavor_text: Tried to pay back every fine owed to the DP World Tour just to get back in the building, including offering nearly £700,000 in total. Turned down, since resigning his membership made him ineligible regardless of the money. Missed his first Ryder Cup since his 1999 debut.

name: Sergio Garcia
flavor_text: Paid over £1 million in fines to rejoin the DP World Tour and earn eligibility back, the all-time Ryder Cup points leader given a real shot at a return. His own form undercut him instead, missing cuts at majors and admitting in May he'd have turned down a pick himself. Withdrew from the Irish Open in disappointment once the call came.

name: Dustin Johnson
flavor_text: Went 5-0-0 at Whistling Straits two years earlier, then resigned his PGA Tour membership for LIV, cutting off the only path to points. Zach Johnson confirmed he only weighed picks inside the top 20-25 on the list, a bar Johnson's move made impossible to clear.
